units.text: INT. HEDGE-WITCH'S COTTAGE - KITCHEN - EVENING
A low-beamed room.
Bunches of dried thyme and nettle hang from the rafters.
A kettle sings on a cast-iron stove.
Through a small window, an orchard is going dark.
I know you are in there! I can hear you chewing!
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Thumping on the stairs.
SERAPHINA QUILL, seventies, small and broad, in a flour-dusted apron, stumps into the kitchen with a broom in one hand.
She stops.
The kitchen is empty.
She looks under the table, behind the door, in the wood-bin.
She scowls.
She lowers the broom.
Fine. Keep it.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: She goes to the stove and moves the kettle off the heat.
She finds a clay cup on the shelf and pours something dark and steaming.
She drinks.
She pulls a stool to the table and sits heavily.
Her eyes drift to a stoppered bottle on the sill.
Inside, a pale blue light pulses once, then dims.
She watches it for a while.
Thirty years, you stubborn thing.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: She takes the bottle down and holds it in both hands.
The light brightens at her touch.
She smiles, tired but real.
Go on, then. I'm too old to keep a ghost in a bottle.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: She pulls the stopper.
The blue light drifts out in a slow curl, circles the kitchen once, kisses the dried thyme, and slips through the glass of the window into the dusk.
She sits there until the cup has gone cold.
Then she gets up, wipes her hands on her apron, and starts to chop an onion.
